title: The leak scan flags the EC armor label quoted before a repository path with a camel-case abbreviation (ConfigMgr, UserSvc), which the old segment-length rule let pass
goal: kbcommon.leak_hits does not flag the EC armor label quoted directly before a repository path with a short camel-case abbreviation such as ConfigMgr or UserSvc, and still flags a single-line EC key body of 20 to 40 characters that holds a slash

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import kbcommon;L="-"*5+"BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY"+"-"*5;bad=[p for p in ("kb/public/mecm/ConfigMgr/Views.md","Docs/ConfigMgr/2203/ReleaseNotes.md","docs/UserSvc/Overview.md") if any(k=="secret" for k,_ in kbcommon.leak_hits(L+" "+p))];print("paths flagged:",bad);sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
